purpose: Provide role-specific interview postures so future sessions do not use one generic grief interview for every kind of witness.
global_prompt_rule: Ask for scenes, language, uncertainty, and context; do not ask contributors to perform wisdom, prove meaning, or supply advice.

protocols.name: adult_family_witness_bereaved_not_fresh
good_first_questions: What do you remember noticing before you had words for it?
What words did people in the room use?
What did you later search for?
What do you wish had been named without being explained away?
do_not_ask: to retell the whole death if one moment is enough
to decide what the dying person meant
publication_cautions: identifiability through rare diagnosis or location

protocols.name: hospice_or_palliative_nurse_practitioner_craft
good_first_questions: What do new families most often panic-search after seeing this?
What phrase do you use that avoids false reassurance?
What detail is in your hands, ears, or nose but not in textbooks?
What should not be turned into public instructions?

protocols.name: hospice_aide_cna_home_health_aide_bodywork
good_first_questions: What does hands-on care notice that other roles miss?
How do linens, skin, mouth, weight, odor, or room arrangement become part of the death?
What words protect dignity?

protocols.name: chaplain_social_worker_doula_presence_language
good_first_questions: What language do families use when they cannot say dying?
What silences are important?
When is a script harmful?
What does presence do that advice cannot?

protocols.name: funeral_director_body_preparation_crematory_cemetery
good_first_questions: What is the second handoff like?
What words do families use when choosing clothing, rings, viewing, or disposition?
What body facts should be named without spectacle?

protocols.name: ems_dispatcher_first_responder_bystander
good_first_questions: What is the first language of sudden death?
What does a caller or responder need named later?
Where does official time begin while family time fractures?

protocols.name: tradition_holder_or_community_review
good_first_questions: What exterior vocabulary may be safely named?
What should be represented only as restricted/refused?
Who has authority to review wording?
What language/diacritics should be preserved?
do_not_ask: for a single person to speak for a whole tradition
for sacred material to become searchable content

protocols.name: survivor_after_cardiac_arrest_or_moribund_recovery
good_first_questions: What do you remember, and what do you not remember?
What language feels accurate without turning it into proof for others?
What did others tell you later that changed your memory?

protocols.name: high_gate_no_contact_domains
allowed_actions: consult specialists/advisors without asking for stories
